title: Ukraine Strikes Shadow Fleet Tankers and Tuapse Oil Complex for 4th Time in 16 Days
detail: Ukrainian forces struck Russian oil-loading infrastructure and hit 2–3 'shadow fleet' tankers allegedly transporting Russian crude in violation of Western sanctions. Ukraine also carried out its fourth strike in 16 days on Rosneft's Tuapse refinery and oil export complex on the Black Sea coast. Earlier strikes at Tuapse had sparked fires severe enough to force local evacuations and cause 'black rain' (oily droplets) over the town, with elevated benzene levels recorded. The campaign is part of Ukraine's strategic targeting of Russian energy export infrastructure to cut war funding. Zelenskyy described the effort as 'a new stage in the use of Ukrainian weapons to limit the potential of Russia's war machine.' The shadow fleet tankers targeted were allegedly engaged in sanctions evasion — transporting Russian crude outside the G7 price cap framework.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes shadow fleet tankers and Tuapse oil terminal for the 4th time in 16 days

title: Zelensky Arrives in Yerevan for 8th European Political Community Summit — First-Ever Visit to Armenia
detail: President Zelensky arrived in Yerevan, Armenia on May 3 for the 8th European Political Community summit — his first-ever visit to the country. The summit brought together 48 European leaders under the theme 'Building the Future: Unity and Stability in Europe.' Zelensky set three key objectives: (1) advancing a 'dignified end to the war'; (2) implementing the EU's €90 billion interest-free loan to Kyiv approved in April 2026; (3) strengthening Ukraine's air defenses and energy infrastructure. He held bilateral meetings with the prime ministers of the UK, Norway, Finland, and Czech Republic. A 'Washington Format' meeting was also held on the sidelines, focused on Ukraine's security situation. The summit represents continued European diplomatic solidarity with Ukraine as ceasefire discussions remain stalled and Russia continues its aerial bombardment campaign.

title: ISW: Ukrainian Forces Advance NW of Orikhiv; 141 Combat Engagements in 24 Hours; Russian Losses Reach 1,334,000+
detail: Per ISW's May 3 assessment, Russian forces in April 2026 suffered a net territorial loss for the first time since Ukraine's August 2024 Kursk incursion — a significant shift in momentum. Ukrainian forces made a confirmed advance northwest of Orikhiv in the Zaporizhzhia direction as of May 3. ISW recorded 141 combat engagements in a single 24-hour period as of May 3 — signaling intensive ongoing frontline activity. Russian cumulative personnel losses since February 24, 2022 reached approximately 1,334,030–1,335,150, with approximately 1,080–1,120 casualties per day in the May 2–4 window. Zelensky separately warned of unusual activity near the Sumy-Belarus border — including new roads and artillery positions being established inside Belarus — suggesting possible planning for a second front, though the threat assessment remained unconfirmed. Russian offensives continued near Pokrovsk, Myrnohrad, and Huliaipole with limited results.

media.caption: ISW May 3 assessment: Ukrainian forces advance NW of Orikhiv; 141 combat engagements recorded; Russian losses exceed 1.334 million
